task: Faster receipt and trip entry: scan receipts on the device, pick dates from a calendar, and choose categories from a list. Keep every existing screen, flow, the local-first design and the current look; keep all existing tests passing. Changes: (1) Receipt scanning (OCR), entirely on the device: after the user takes or chooses a receipt photo, read its text with expo-text-extractor ^2.0.0 (Apple Vision on iOS, ML Kit on Android; no network, no cloud). Put it behind src/lib/ocr.ts with recognizeReceiptText(uri) and a pure parseReceipt(text) that returns {merchant, date, total, tax} with each field optional (find the total from lines like TOTAL / AMOUNT DUE / BALANCE, not SUBTOTAL; dates in common US formats; merchant from the first meaningful line). Pre-fill the receipt form with what was found, mark the pre-filled fields with "Check these details" until the user edits or confirms them, and never save automatically. If nothing is found, say so and let the user type the details. On the web, and wherever text recognition is unavailable, the scan button explains "Scanning is available in the phone app" and the manual form still works. Unit-test parseReceipt with at least 8 realistic receipt texts (grocery, fuel, restaurant with tip, hardware store, online order, faded/partial text, a receipt with several dates, one with no total); mock expo-text-extractor in Jest via __mocks__. (2) Date picker: replace typed dates on receipts and mileage entries with react-native-paper-dates ^0.24.1 (a date field that opens a calendar; today by default; no future dates for receipts). (3) Categories: the receipt category is a dropdown pre-loaded with Advertising & marketing, Vehicle & fuel, Meals, Travel & lodging, Office supplies, Software & subscriptions, Phone & internet, Equipment & tools, Professional services, Insurance, Education & training, Bank & payment fees, Other. The dropdown's last option "Add category..." lets the user add their own (1-40 characters, no duplicates ignoring case). Settings gets "Categories" to rename or hide categories; a category used by any receipt can't be deleted, only hidden. Custom categories and changes are stored encrypted through the Store and included in backups and restores (older backups without categories still restore, with the defaults). Existing receipts keep their category text; a category not in the list is added as a custom one. Add unit tests for categories (defaults, add, duplicate, rename, hide, in-use protection, backup round trip) and update ui_flow.json so the primary flow picks a date from the calendar and a category from the dropdown, and adds a custom category.

security.summary: The latest changes (OCR, date picker, and category management) did not introduce any new critical or high severity code issues. All existing high‑severity code findings remain addressed (data‑reset‑photo‑leak has been fixed). The open medium‑severity findings from the previous review (backup size DOS, passphrase brute‑force, CSV injection, passphrase length, photo path traversal) are unchanged. ui.summary: The UI implements the primary flow and passes all axe accessibility checks, with a Lighthouse accessibility score of 98 and no console errors. Navigation works from every signed‑in screen (bottom tab bar is present) and the main states (policy gate, dashboard empty, receipt entry, mileage entry, settings, categories) are reachable. However, a few secondary states and design‑token inconsistencies are missing or incomplete, and some interaction‑state styling (focus outlines) does not fully meet the spec. These issues are not show‑stoppers for the core flow but should be fixed to reach a truly polished product.

findings.issue: The dashboard loading state (full‑screen centered ActivityIndicator) is defined in DESIGN.md but is never rendered – the screen jumps straight to the empty or populated view.
findings.fix: Add a conditional render that shows <ActivityIndicator size="large" /> centered when the dashboard data is being fetched, and hide it once data is available.

findings.issue: The dropdown placeholder text "Select category" is hard‑coded instead of using a token or the label prop, and the component does not apply the design token spacing for the menu items.
findings.fix: Expose a `placeholder` prop that defaults to the token‑based string from DESIGN.md and use `theme.spacing` for menu item padding/margin to stay consistent with the 8 dp grid.

findings.issue: Visible focus styling (2 dp outline using `theme.colors.outline`) is missing on web – only the ripple effect appears on native platforms.
findings.fix: Add a `:focus-visible` CSS rule (or Paper’s `style` prop) that sets a 2 dp solid outline with `theme.colors.outline` and ensures the outline is also applied when navigating with the keyboard.

findings.issue: Bottom navigation tabs lack explicit `aria-label` and `role="navigation"` attributes on the web, which can hinder screen‑reader navigation despite passing axe.
findings.fix: Wrap the `BottomNavigation` in a `<nav aria-label="Primary navigation">` element and add `accessibilityLabel`/`accessibilityRole` props to each tab to convey their purpose to assistive tech.

findings.issue: Several components (e.g., `EmptyState` action button, `MiniFAB` background) use hard‑coded hex colors (`#0061A4`, `#015958`) instead of the exported design tokens.
findings.fix: Replace the literal color values with references to `theme.colors.primary`, `theme.colors.secondary`, etc., and ensure the CSS file mirrors those tokens for the web build.

findings.issue: Horizontal padding is set to a literal `16` dp instead of using `theme.spacing * 2` as defined in the layout spec.
findings.fix: Update the style to `paddingHorizontal: theme.spacing * 2` (or the CSS custom property `var(--spacing-unit) * 2`).

findings.issue: The OCR loading overlay shows the spinner but does not include the required label "Analyzing receipt…" for live announcements.
findings.fix: Add a `<Text>` element beside the `ActivityIndicator` with the exact copy and mark it with `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` so screen readers announce the loading state.

findings.issue: Typography lacks a real type scale: the title 'Nothing here yet' is the same size as the description text, and both are larger than the primary button text, creating a visual hierarchy that doesn't clearly prioritize the primary action.
findings.fix: Adjust font sizes to create a clear typographic hierarchy: use a larger, bolder font for the primary headline, a smaller font for the description, and a consistent, slightly smaller size for the button text.

findings.issue: Secondary buttons 'Receipt' and 'Mileage' are visually inconsistent with the primary 'Add receipt' button: they are smaller, lack the same visual weight, and are positioned to the right, which breaks the expected left-aligned grouping.
findings.fix: Align the secondary buttons with the primary button and make them visually consistent in size, weight, and styling. Consider using a smaller but still distinct button style to differentiate them from the primary action.

findings.issue: On desktop, the secondary buttons are positioned too far to the right, creating an unbalanced layout and leaving large empty space on the left side.
findings.fix: Center the secondary buttons horizontally or group them with the primary button in a consistent, balanced layout that respects the desktop viewport width.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'dashboard_empty' (target 8+, minimum 7): Polished and functional empty state with clear primary action. Good visual hierarchy and spacing, but typography lacks a real scale and the secondary buttons feel inconsistent in placement and styling.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

improvements.title: Add pre‑coding export validation to catch missing module exports
improvements.evidence: Round 1 failed the `typescript (tsc)` validator: missing exported members `createBackup`, `restoreBackup`, `validateBackupStructure`, `deleteCategory` (see raw_output round 1). The coder hit its turn limit (64 calls) and spent ~14 min before the issue was discovered.
improvements.change: Static validator (validate.py) – introduce an `export_check` step that parses all test imports and the DESIGN.md to build a required‑exports list per file. Run this validator **before** the coder starts (round 0). If any export is missing, fail with a clear message and a stub implementation suggestion.
improvements.expected_effect: Missing exports are detected early, eliminating wasted coder turns and preventing turn‑limit hits. Convergence speeds up because the coder can start with a correct module skeleton.

improvements.title: Make reviewer feedback actionable with file paths and stub code
improvements.evidence: Reviewer issues in round 1 were generic (e.g., "Missing exported functions createBackup…") leading to the coder’s trial‑and‑error (64 calls). Round 2 still required a separate fix for the passphrase validator, adding 42 min of work.
improvements.change:
Reviewer prompt – require feedback in the form:
```
File: src/lib/backup.ts
Add export const createBackup = async (store, passphrase) => { /* stub */ };
```
Include line numbers and short code snippets for every issue (exports, validation logic, etc.).
improvements.expected_effect: Coder receives precise, ready‑to‑copy fixes, reducing the number of iterations and overall round time.

improvements.title: Enforce a detailed implementation blueprint in the planner output
improvements.evidence: The coder consumed 1 859 113 prompt tokens in round 1 and hit the turn limit, indicating an under‑specified plan. The missing backup exports and the ambiguous validation logic were not listed in the planner’s initial plan.
improvements.change:
Planner prompt – add a requirement to output a table of all new/modified files with exact function signatures and required export statements. Example:
| File | Exported symbols | Signature |
|------|-----------------|-----------|
| src/lib/backup.ts | createBackup, restoreBackup, validateBackupStructure, deleteCategory | async (store: Store, passphrase: string) => Promise<string> |
Pass this blueprint as the first context for the coder.
improvements.expected_effect: Provides a clear, low‑entropy roadmap, reduces token usage, and prevents missing‑export bugs, leading to faster convergence.

improvements.title: Run targeted unit tests for critical validators early
improvements.evidence: Round 2 failed the passphrase validation test (`validateBackupPassphrase('exactly12!!')` returned an error) after a long 42 min iteration. The bug stemmed from an off‑by‑one length check.
improvements.change: Add a lightweight validator step that runs the `passphraseRules.test.ts` unit test before the coder begins work on the backup module. If it fails, surface the exact expected behavior (minimum length = 12) to the coder.
improvements.expected_effect: Detects the boundary‑condition bug before any coding, avoiding the 42‑minute round 2 delay.

improvements.title: Split large tasks into focused phases with lower turn limits
improvements.evidence: Coder hit its turn limit in round 1 (64 calls) and overall round 2 lasted 2554 s (≈43 min). The combined tasks (backup refactor, OCR addition, date picker, category UI) overloaded a single round.
improvements.change: Planner – break the overall feature set into separate phases (e.g., "Backup API fixes", "Passphrase validation", "OCR & date picker integration", "Category UI updates"). For each phase set a tighter turn limit (≈30 turns) and restart the coder with the phase‑specific blueprint.
improvements.expected_effect: Prevents turn‑limit exhaustion, keeps each round short and focused, and improves overall pipeline throughput.
